sections.heading: Sarhad Dairy: The Kutch District Milk Union
paragraphs: Sarhad Dairy is the brand of the Kutch District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union, a member union of GCMMF, the Amul federation. IANS reported in January 2026 that it works through more than 900 village societies, collects about 5.5 lakh litres a day from roughly 80,000 producers and processes about 4 lakh litres a day.

The same report credits the union with a 300-tonne cattle feed plant, ice cream output of about 50,000 litres a day with a peak of 3.38 lakh litres a day, a 2024-25 turnover above Rs 1,200 crore at annual growth of 9.09 per cent, and buffalo milk supplied to Amul plants in Haryana, Telangana and Maharashtra.

sections.heading: Camel Milk Processing in Kutch
paragraphs: IANS describes Sarhad's camel milk operation as the first camel milk processing plant in India, with a deodorisation facility in use since 16 January 2019. Camel milk is collected through centres at Rapar, Nakhatrana, Gadhshisha and Kotda Athamana, averaged 4,754 litres a day in 2024-25, and earned more than 350 herding families Rs 8.72 crore that year.

A camel-milk ice cream plant was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 22 February 2024 and makes 80 varieties. IANS puts its 2024-25 output at 24.52 lakh litres, with peak dispatch of 58,000 litres.

sections.heading: The Planned Anjar Processing Unit
paragraphs: DairyNews reported in December 2020 that the Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for a Rs 121 crore Sarhad unit at Anjar of 2 lakh litres a day, designed to be expandable to 4 lakh litres, for buttermilk, kheer, rabdi and curd. The report said the plant would remove the need to send surplus milk about 350 km to Gandhinagar. We have not found a later source confirming its commissioning, so it is described here as announced.

If the Anjar unit goes ahead, its curd, buttermilk and dessert lines would be new product-contact pipework, and a buyer planning that work can send line sizes early so finish and certification are agreed before fabrication starts.

sections.heading: Specifying Tube for Kutch Dairy and Ice Cream Lines
paragraphs: Ice cream mix, cultured products such as curd and buttermilk, and the low-volume camel milk lines are where cleanability decides tube choice, so we supply 316L to ASTM A270 with an SF4 electropolished bore for product contact. Every electropolished lot carries an Ra report and an EN 10204 3.1 certificate traced to the heat number.
Chilling, cattle feed plant water services and CIP return headers rarely need that finish, and SF1 or mill-finish 304L keeps those runs economical.

sections.heading: What to Send With a Kutch Enquiry
bullets: Line served: chilling, pasteuriser, ice cream, curd and buttermilk, camel milk or CIP
Outside diameter, wall thickness and total metres for each size
Grade and internal finish: 316L SF4, 304L SF1 or mill finish
Standard to be met: ASTM A270, A269 or ASME BPE
Bends, tees, ferrules or reducers required with the tube

sections.heading: Delivery to Bhuj, Anjar and the Rest of Kutch
paragraphs: Kutch orders move by road from Mumbai, with every electropolished length capped and sleeved, and we put the dispatch date and transit in writing once the order is confirmed. Each length is PMI-tested before dispatch, and a complete enquiry receives a quotation within 24 hours.
